See spikes/s2-parse-perf/README.md.

title: 1.3 MetadataGraph: canonical IDs, evidence records, Unresolved records
description: Design section 5. Logical-to-physical edges; every edge carries origin, confidence, artifact_version, location. Addresses review F07 and F09.
close_reason: MetadataGraph in lineagepilot_core.graph. IDs per design 5.1: unique_id, relation:<db>.<schema>.<name> (prefixed so physical IDs cannot collide with dbt IDs), <node>#<column>, airflow:<dag>.<task>; names folded to the adapter's case rules (Snowflake upper unless quoted, others lower). Edges point upstream to downstream (depends_on, derives, materialises, orchestrates, task_depends_on) and carry a list of Evidence (origin, confidence, ArtifactVersion with path/sha256/generated_at/dbt_version, Location); the same edge from two sources keeps both. Logical-to-physical mappings are explicit materialises edges, so a source and a model on one table meet at one relation (F09). Unresolved records carry evidence (F07); column names that collide under case rules become Unresolved. The parser now records manifest and catalog sha256. build_dbt_graph refuses a parse with errors (UntrustedParseResult), so an untrusted index cannot look complete. 5,000 models: parse 2.2-2.4 s plus build 0.3 s; graph allocations about 50 MB.

title: 1.4 Traversal and impact query at model and column level
description: Upstream/downstream, depth caps, cycle safety. Rewrite over the in-memory graph (fixes review F06 by construction).
close_reason: lineagepilot_core.analysis: traverse() (BFS up/down at model or column level, depth and node caps with a truncated flag, cycle-safe, all ways in recorded) and impact() (design section 8 step 4). Physical tables are junctions: a source is downstream of the models/seeds/snapshots that build its table, so jaffle seeds reach marts through their sources (F09); Airflow tasks that run a node are downstream of it. Impact follows derives edges where a model's column lineage is resolved/partial, falls back to model level marked inferred where it is unknown or not computed (with the reason), and reaches exposures and tasks that use the whole node; confidence is the strongest path's weakest evidence; unknowns on targets and impacted nodes (and their columns) are listed. A column_lineage callback lets callers compute lineage on demand. 5,000 models: model impact from the worst source (651 nodes) 3-5 ms; all columns of it 16-25 ms. Python 3.10 GC pauses of 200-285 ms vanish with gc.freeze() after load; noted in design 11 and LP-243.1.

title: 1.5 Rules engine: five result states, coverage-aware score, rule packs
description: pass/fail/not_applicable/unsupported/unknown; unsupported and unknown excluded from the denominator; 12 carried + 6 remapped rules; .lineagepilot/rules.yml packs with length-capped, time-limited regexes (carries the ReDoS lesson from closed DCS-61r).
close_reason: lineagepilot_core.rules: five results (pass, fail, not_applicable, unsupported, unknown); score excludes unsupported/unknown from the denominator, with coverage and a severity-weighted score beside it (F11). 18 built-in rules: MED_001-005, DBT_001-004, PII_001-003 carried with legacy IDs/severities/remediations, and DBT_005-010 remapping DIM2_006, DIM4_002, DIM4_004, DIM4_001, DIM3_005, DIM3_006 to dbt facts (unique+not_null tests or a contract primary key; unique test; relationships test; gold has tests; meta.owner or group; meta.domain). Behaviour fixes: MED_001/002 report unknown for upstreams without a layer or unresolved deps (server passed them); DBT_003 is case-sensitive (server matched IGNORECASE). Findings carry evidence: manifest artifact, location (schema.yml for documentation rules), and heuristic confidence when a layer or PII type was guessed from a pattern. Custom rules from .lineagepilot/rules.yml (F10): 256 KB cap, 200 rules, field-by-field validation, disable and severity overrides, unknown checks become unsupported; regexes length-capped (200), refused if they can backtrack exponentially (nested repeats, alternation in a repeat, backreferences), subjects capped at 512 chars, and a pattern slower than 50 ms is switched off (DCS-61r). Parser records layer_source and contract primary keys. 5,000 models: evaluate 0.26-0.29 s.

title: 1.6 PII indicators tracing all upstream paths
description: Label as indicators, not verified exposure (review F12).
close_reason: lineagepilot_core.analysis.pii: indicators that are declared (tag), suggested by a column name (pattern) or inherited along every lineage path (lineage), propagated over derives edges and across physical tables (seed -> source) with a worklist to a fixed point, so every path contributes its origins (F12; the server followed edges[0]). Masked columns stop the flow; downstream models with unknown/uncomputed column lineage are listed as unknown, never clean. pii_exposure: unmasked indicators in consumption layers with severity (legacy map), reasons naming the basis, and consumers (exposures, Airflow tasks). trace_pii: all upstream origins, downstream flow, masked_at, terminals, unknowns. All labelled indicators, not verified exposure. Pattern fixes: ip_address no longer claimed by address; city/state/country/zip/postal are location (MEDIUM), not HIGH address (S2 finding j). 5,000 models: index + exposure 0.23-0.40 s.

title: 1.8 Snapshot cache and headless CLI (lineagepilot index / impact)
description: Snapshot keyed by manifest hash in storageUri; headless entry point reused by CI later.
close_reason: Snapshot cache and headless CLI. snapshot.py: whole-graph JSON snapshots (artifacts and evidence interned in tables), keyed by manifest and catalog sha256 + snapshot format + core version + column-lineage flag; atomic writes; any malformed, tampered or mismatched snapshot is refused and rebuilt; SnapshotCache keeps the newest 3 as baselines. indexer.py: one pipeline (snapshot or parse, graph, column lineage, snapshot) for the CLI and the Phase 2 indexer; untrusted artifacts give an unknown index and are never cached. cli.py: lineagepilot index / impact (targets by unique_id, model name, file path or model#column), text or --json, exit codes 0/1/2. Warm start at 5,000 models with full column lineage: 0.53-0.56 s, peak 387-405 MB after pausing GC during load and releasing records as they are consumed (from 1.13-1.36 s and 457-483 MB). scripts/budgets.py reproduces every design section 11 budget.

title: 1.9 Column lineage with sqlglot.lineage and a catalog.json schema
description: S2 found the existing sql_column_parser returns a single '*' for 86-100% of compiled dbt models, so design section 6.1's reuse plan does not work. Build column lineage on sqlglot.lineage with a schema from catalog.json (S2: 91-99% of columns resolved, <=0.35 s per model). Models without a catalog or that fail to parse are 'unknown', never 'no lineage'. Pin sqlglot's major version.
close_reason: Column lineage on sqlglot.lineage: parsers/sql_lineage.py (pure: SQL + catalog MappingSchema -> per-output-column sources with passthrough/transform/aggregate) and graph/column_lineage.py (derives edges with compiled_sql/inferred evidence; per-model resolved/partial/unknown status; Unresolved records; recomputable per model). Unknown with a reason for: no compiled SQL, no catalog, Python model, unparseable SQL, non-query, SQL over 1M chars, a table not in the catalog, an unexpandable *, sqlglot failure. compiled_sql() reads manifest compiled_code or target/compiled under the project root, refusing paths that leave it. Measured: prebuilt MappingSchema and trim_selects=False cut sqlglot from 79 ms to about 3 ms per model. jaffle-shop: 13/13 resolved, 87 derives edges, spot-checked by hand. 5,000 synthetic models: 5,000 resolved, 99.6% of output columns traced (rest are constants), full pass 20.5 s on 3.13 and 28.6 s on 3.10, so it runs after the model-level index (recorded in design section 11). sqlglot stays pinned to major 30.

title: HTML and CSV reports: stored HTML injection and formula injection
description: api/routers/reports.py builds HTML with f-strings and no escaping (381-384, 405-408, 428-435, 550-554): column/capsule names, pii_type, layer, data_type, rule_name, subject_name, message. Served as attachment, so payload runs when the saved .html is opened (file://, no CSP) and can exfiltrate the PII inventory. CSV output (98-115, 199-214, 294-312) quotes correctly but does not neutralise cells starting with = + - @ TAB CR. Fix: html.escape every value or Jinja2 autoescape=True, add restrictive meta CSP; prefix apostrophe on formula-leading CSV cells.
close_reason: Fixed in lineagepilot_core.export (task 1.7). The HTML report is retired with the server (design section 7 offers Markdown and CSV only). CSV cells starting with = + - @ TAB CR get a leading apostrophe and NULs are dropped (Python 3.10's csv module crashed on them; found by the property test); Markdown cells escape &, <, > and Markdown markup and collapse line breaks, so names cannot inject HTML or links. Property tests re-read both formats.

title: Cypher export injection: unescaped URNs in relationship MATCH statements
description: services/graph_export.py:729-733 interpolates edge.source_urn/target_urn into double-quoted Cypher strings. URNs embed attacker-controlled dbt model names and domain/tag/product names. A model named x"}) RETURN 1; MATCH (n) DETACH DELETE n; MATCH (a {urn: "y produces a statement that wipes the target Neo4j DB when the exported script is run (cypher-shell -f / Browser). Same path via CLI (cli/main.py:1193). Fix: json.dumps the URNs as node properties already do, or emit parameterised UNWIND $rows; whitelist labels and rel types.
close_reason: Fixed in lineagepilot_core.export (task 1.7): every Cypher value is a JSON-escaped string literal (valid Cypher, ASCII-only), nodes MERGE on id then SET a label from a fixed map, relationship types come from a fixed map, unknown kinds are skipped, and no data appears in comments. Regression test with the DETACH DELETE payload; hypothesis property test checks every statement matches the template and every literal decodes to the original value.

title: Graph export encoding: GraphML/DOT/Mermaid injection and Content-Disposition filename
description: graph_export.py: GraphML writes node.layer/domain unescaped (611-612; element injection, ill-formed XML); DOT puts layer raw in subgraph name and label and leaves IDs unquoted (665-691); Mermaid uses raw layer and URN IDs and does not strip newlines (752-773). graph.py:189-201 builds Content-Disposition filename from the URN tail (parameter injection; non-Latin-1 names cause a 500 and break the lineage view). Fix: escape all interpolated values per format, use generated node IDs (n0, n1...), restrict filename to [A-Za-z0-9_-] and add RFC 5987 filename*.
close_reason: Fixed in lineagepilot_core.export (task 1.7): GraphML is built with ElementTree after removing characters XML 1.0 cannot carry; DOT and Mermaid use generated IDs (n0, n1, ...) with every label quoted and escaped (DOT backslashes, Mermaid entity-encodes everything but plain text, so no newline, click line or %% directive survives); layer names go through the same escaping. There is no HTTP server, so Content-Disposition is gone; safe_filename() restricts export file names to [A-Za-z0-9_-]. Property tests re-parse GraphML (ElementTree), DOT (pydot) and Mermaid (strict line grammar).
